survivorship_bias_note: Most visible binary cases are enforcement actions, bans and scam exposures. Retail winners are rare, self-reported and unverifiable, so they are absent here. Regulator studies show most retail lose, but winners publicise selectively. Treat any 80-90% win-rate claim as marketing.

why_how_where.why: Payout below fair odds (80-90% payout with ~50% hit rate is negative expectancy); short expiry is mostly noise; offshore brokers were often counterparty or outright fraud.
why_how_where.how: Fixed payout, very short expiry, high frequency, martingale sizing, blocked withdrawals. Regulated route: listed, collateralised contracts with fixed risk.
why_how_where.where: Offshore online brokers (Cyprus, Israel) now banned in EU, UK, Australia, Israel; US legal only on CFTC-regulated venues; 2025-26 revival as short-dated crypto prediction-market contracts.

engine_notes: Treat expiry under 1h as high noise; require edge net of spread and payout.

trade_cases.pnl_note: Regulator view built from complaints and provider data, not a random sample of all users.
trade_cases.why_what: ESMA banned marketing/sale of binary options to retail clients (temporary measure 2018, EUR-Lex Decision 2018/795), citing negative expected returns and fraud/manipulation concerns.
trade_cases.how: Product intervention under MiFIR Art 40; analysis says expected retail return is negative given payout below fair odds, and the provider is usually the counterparty.
trade_cases.lesson: Fixed payout below fair odds gives negative expectancy; need edge above breakeven hit rate.
trade_cases.survivorship_note: Regulator view built from complaints and provider data, not a random sample of all users.
